# Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience

> **Headline:** Add a versioned, bot-baseline-derived **intended-experience
> targets** artifact plus a deterministic **human-experience validation**
> command that compares measured human (and bot) balance statistics against
> those bands, emitting a versioned JSON report and Markdown summary and
> failing with a non-zero exit code on drift.

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature · **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

Balancing is currently a manual, point-in-time activity. The automated-balancing
framework produces a stable, versioned `BalanceReport`, and the human-play
statistics work item produces the *same* statistics for real players — but
nothing states what the experience is *supposed* to be, and nothing periodically
checks the measured experience against it. This item turns the bot batch into
the **source of truth for intended experience** (recorded as explicit target
bands and mirrored into the GDD), then adds a repeatable validation that flags
drift in the measured human experience.

## Users

- **As a game designer / producer**, I want a periodic report comparing the
  measured human experience against explicit intended-experience targets, so I
  can see whether the game still plays as designed and where it has drifted.
- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want the intended experience written
  down as machine-checkable targets derived from a bot baseline, so a tuning
  change can be judged against a recorded standard rather than remembered.
- **As a maintainer**, I want the same validation to run against a fresh bot
  batch, so a regression in the balance baseline is caught even before any human
  play is recorded.
- **As a producer**, I want a durable, versioned pass/fail artifact, so the
  experience of the game can be reviewed over time.

## Intended-experience definition (decision recorded)

The operator chose the **bot baseline** as the source of intended-experience
targets, with the **GDD updated to match**. Concretely:

- A bot batch (`npm run evaluate -- --batch`) produces the shared
  `BalanceAggregate`. Its per-metric distributions define the **target band**
  (centre = baseline mean/median; tolerance = a documented multiple of std-dev
  or a relative percentage).
- The resulting bands are committed as a **versioned targets artifact** — the
  single machine-checkable statement of intended experience.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` is updated so the *prose* intended experience
  (survival, pacing, progression, reward cadence) agrees with those bands.

This keeps one source of truth (the artifact) and one narrative (the GDD).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Versioned, machine-checkable targets.** A targets artifact (e.g.
   `src/data/experience-targets.json`) records, for each key metric of the
   shared `BalanceAggregate` schema — at minimum `survivalSeconds`,
   `mineralsCollected`, `upgradesSelected`, `waveReached`, `levelReached` and
   `avoidableHits` — a target band (centre + tolerance) plus a version
   constant, seeded from a recorded bot batch baseline. A test asserts the
   artifact validates against the schema and covers every required metric.
- **Pure comparator.** A pure, clock-free, I/O-free module compares a
   `BalanceAggregate` (human **or** bot) against the targets and returns, per
   metric, the measured value, the target band, the signed drift magnitude and
   a pass/fail verdict. Unit tests cover in-band, above-band, below-band,
   missing-metric and empty-input cases, and assert no I/O / clock access.
- **Periodic validation command.** A documented on-demand command (e.g.
   `npm run validate-experience -- <balance-report.json>`) reads a
   `BalanceReport`, compares it against the targets, writes a **versioned JSON
   report** and a **Markdown summary**, and **exits non-zero when any metric
   drifts beyond tolerance**. It labels the source (human / bot policy) in the
   output. Its scheduling (e.g. a documented cron/CI recipe) is documented but
   not built as CI infrastructure in this item.
- **Determinism and reproducibility.** The same input report + targets yields
   byte-identical JSON and Markdown output; the pure core never reads the wall
   clock. Verified by tests (run twice, diff).
- **GDD, documentation and test suite.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` is
   updated so the intended experience matches the bot-baseline-derived targets;
   the validation workflow, targets artifact and report shape are documented
   (extending `docs/BALANCING.md` and/or a new `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md`
   plus code comments/README as applicable); and the **full project test suite
   passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Delivered dependency:** this item depends on **Collect balance statistics
  from human player games (dev mode only)** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN), which is
  now **completed**, together with its helper child AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT
  (`src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts` exists). The human `BalanceReport` this
  validation consumes is therefore available; implementation may proceed.
- Reuse the shared schema (`BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`,
  `BalanceRunStats`, `BalanceAggregate`, `BalanceReport`) — no schema
  duplication.
- **Dev tooling only:** the targets artifact and validator are development
  tooling; no production game-code call site, no telemetry/consent change.
- Deterministic and byte-stable output; the pure core must not read the wall
  clock or perform I/O.
- No wall-clock/network dependency in the comparator; the `--batch` path is
  already reproducible and must stay so.

## Existing state

- **Shared schema:** `src/ai/eval/types.ts` defines `DistributionStats`,
  `BalanceRunStats`, `BalanceAggregate`, `BalanceReport`,
  `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION` and `EVAL_DATASET_VERSION`
  (AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ, completed).
- **Bot batch:** `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` + `scripts/evaluate.mjs` write a
  byte-stable `balance-report.json` / `.txt` / `runs.jsonl` under `--out`
  (default `eval-output/`), documented in `docs/BALANCING.md`. A recorded
  100-game baseline exists in that document's acceptance-verification section.
- **Human stats (delivered):** **Collect balance statistics from human
  player games** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN, completed) emits a `BalanceReport`
  labelled with a `human` pseudo-policy. Its helper
  (`src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts`, AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT) is present.
- **No targets, comparator or validation command exists today.**
- **Related tuning loop:** **Automate the balance-tuning loop** (
  AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715, open) covers baseline/compare for *tuning*; this item
  covers *periodic experience validation* against a committed standard.

## Desired change

1. Add a versioned targets artifact (schema + initial bot-baseline values) and
   a loader/validator.
2. Add a pure comparator module producing per-metric drift + verdicts.
3. Add the validation CLI and a `package.json` script.
4. Add the JSON + Markdown report writers (byte-stable).
5. Add tests (schema, comparator, CLI, determinism) and update docs + GDD.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — add target/drift types + version constant (or a new
  `experienceTargets.ts`).
- `src/ai/eval/experienceTargets.ts` — pure targets loader + comparator
  (new).
- `src/data/experience-targets.json` — versioned intended-experience bands
  seeded from a bot baseline (new; exact path TBD at implementation).
- `src/ai/eval/experienceTargets.test.ts` — schema + comparator unit tests
  (new).
- `scripts/validate-experience.mjs` (+ `.d.mts`) — validation CLI (new).
- `scripts/validate-experience.test.ts` — CLI + determinism tests (new).
- `package.json` — add the validation script.
- `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md` and/or `docs/BALANCING.md` — document the
  workflow, targets and report shape.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — align the stated intended experience with
  the targets.

## Related work

- **Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) — epic that delivered the
  schema and batch runner.
- **Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)**
  (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — supplies the human statistics (dependency).
- **Shared human balance-statistics helper** (AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT) — the
  helper this item depends on indirectly.
- **Balance statistics schema and pure aggregation** (AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ) —
  the shared schema.
- **Automate the balance-tuning loop: baseline, single-edit, re-run and diff**
  (AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715) — related baseline/compare tooling.
- Docs: `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`,
  `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/TELEMETRY.md`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the bot batch is a *directional* proxy for the human
  experience (documented fidelity boundary in `docs/BALANCING.md`). Target
  bands are therefore intentionally tolerant; an out-of-band *human* result is
  a prompt to investigate, not proof of a bug.
- **Risk (dependency):** implementation is blocked until the human-stats item
  lands; the brief can be finalised now but must not proceed to implementation.
- **Risk (target inflation):** deriving targets from the bot baseline makes the
  bot trivially self-consistent; the comparator's value is against *human*
  stats. Document this explicitly so a green bot run is not mistaken for proof
  of a good human experience.
- **Risk (tolerance tuning):** too-tight bands cause false drift alarms; too
  loose hide real regressions. Mitigation: state the tolerance rule in the
  artifact and document how to adjust it.
- **Scope-creep risk:** CI scheduling, dashboards and automatic ticket creation
  on drift are *out of scope*; scheduling is documented only.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Where should the initial *intended-experience targets* come from?**
  — Answer (operator, interactive): **Bot baseline, and update the GDD to
  match.** The bot batch's aggregate distributions define the target bands; the
  GDD is edited so its prose intended experience agrees. Source: interactive
  reply.
- **Q: What form should the "periodic" run take?**
  — Answer (operator): **As recommended** — an on-demand, deterministic
  validation command with documented scheduling (no CI cron infra is added in
  this item; the repo has none today). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: What should the validation emit?**
  — Answer (operator): **Versioned JSON + Markdown summary + exit code**
  (non-zero on drift). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: What is the current state of the shared schema and human stats?**
  — Answer (agent, research): The shared schema is delivered
  (`src/ai/eval/types.ts`, AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ); the human-stats collection is
  still open (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) and its helper
  (`src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts`, AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT) does not exist. This item
  is consequently `blocked` for implementation. Research: `wl show` +
  `ls src/ai/eval/`. Source: repository.
- **Q: Does a targets artifact or validator already exist?**
  — Answer (agent, research): No. Research: `ls src/ai/eval/`, `grep` of
  `docs/BALANCING.md`. Source: repository.

**Revision (plan review):** The human-stats dependency
(AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) and its helper (AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT) are now
**completed** (`src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts` present). The earlier "blocked"
constraint above is superseded by this revision; planning proceeded on the
now-unblocked content. Re-verified that no targets artifact
(`src/data/experience-targets.json`) and no validation CLI
(`scripts/validate-experience.mjs`) exist yet.

## Plan: changelog

- Plan review auto-complete path (effort Small / risk Low, below the
  decomposition threshold): six automated review stages run against existing
  content, AC coverage review returned `proceed`. Corrections applied:
  dependency status refreshed from `blocked` to `delivered` in Constraints,
  Existing state, and the Appendix. No feature children created — the item is
  a single small, well-defined vertical slice suitable for direct
  implementation.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW** – Automated Balancing (completed)
- **AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN** – Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only) (open)
- **AH-0MV8ISO4O002HHDT** – Shared human balance-statistics helper (blocked)

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: access, activity, add, added, adds (+263 more)

# Enemies should be aware of the wrap around

## Problem statement

Enemies are currently "wrap-blind": aimed shots always fire a straight line at
the player's raw position (never crossing a screen edge), and enemy movement is
bounded or clamped to the arena, so no enemy ever flies over a screen edge the
way the player ship, asteroids, bullets and the raider patrol already do. The
playfield seam is therefore one-directional — only the player's shots and the
player can cross it — letting the player camp the edges with impunity. Enemy
behaviour should be wrap-aware by default — firing across the seam to reach the
player and flying over the edges — controlled by a per-enemy parameter so a
small set of classic arcade archetypes (Space Invaders march, Centipede) keeps
its bounded, wall-respecting behaviour.

## Users

- **Players** — enemy shots can now arrive from anywhere, including from
  "off-screen" across the seam, so camping a screen edge is no longer a safe
  position. Most enemies occupy the whole wrap-around world rather than a
  bounded box, while the classic set pieces (Space Invaders, Centipede) stay
  recognisible.
- **AI agents / human developers** — one unambiguous data-driven per-archetype
  parameter (`wrapAware`, default `true`) that the game and every gym read
  through the same shared seams, so game↔gym parity is preserved by
  construction and tuning an archetype is a one-field change.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want enemies to fire at me across the screen edge, so that
  hiding against an edge is no longer a guaranteed safe position and shots can
  arrive from the seam exactly like my own wrapped bullets.
- As a **player**, I want most enemies to fly over a screen edge and reappear on
  the opposite side, so the whole wrapped playfield — not a bounded box — is
  part of the arena.
- As a **player**, I want the Space Invaders block and the Centipede to keep
  their classic behaviour (reversing at the walls / weaving within the arena),
  so those recognisable set pieces remain intact.
- As a **developer**, I want a single data-driven `wrapAware` parameter per
  archetype (default: aware) that behaves identically in the game and every
  gym, so enabling or disabling seam-awareness is a one-field change with no
  divergent copies.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Parameter** — Each enemy archetype carries a data-driven boolean
   `wrapAware` (or equivalently named) parameter, defaulting to `true`, wired
   through the existing `EnemyConfig` pipeline so it is visible and editable in
   the enemy editor panel. The `march` (Space Invaders) and `centipede` seed
   configs set it to `false`.
2. **Seam-aware aimed fire** — Aimed shots (Scout, march and the raider's
   aimed fire — every archetype routed through the aimed-shot method) fire
   along the shortest wrapped path to the player: when the direct line is
   longer than the wrap-around route, the shot leaves one edge and arrives from
   the opposite edge (enemy bullets already wrap; AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0). An
   enemy with `wrapAware: false` keeps the current direct aim.
3. **Wrap-aware movement** — Wrap-aware enemy motion (dive, chase, orbit,
   drift, roam, hold-and-move, etc.) that would carry the enemy off-screen
   wraps to the opposite edge (matching the player/asteroid four-edge wrap
   model) instead of being clamped. Non-aware archetypes (`march`,
   `centipede`) are unchanged: march reverses and drops at the arena edge;
   centipede weaves within bounds.
4. **Gym ↔ game parity** — The behaviour is implemented once in the shared
   core (`src/scenes/core/`) and exercised by the affected gym scene(s) and
   `PlayScene` in the same change, so the repo-wide duplicate-body / parity
   guards stay green.
5. **Testing, validation & docs** — Unit tests cover: seam-aware aim angle for
   wrap-aware enemies vs. direct aim for non-aware enemies; position wrapping
   on crossing each edge for wrap-aware motion; config default / CSV wiring
   including the `march` / `centipede` exclusions. The affected documentation
   (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` and any config-format docs) is
   updated to reflect the change. The full project test suite passes with the
   new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the bullet wrap model itself — enemy bullets already wrap and
  expire by lifetime (AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0); this item changes launch direction
  and enemy movement only.
- Exclusions are an explicit seed-config list: only `march` and `centipede`
  default to non-aware. During planning, any other archetype whose classic
  design requires wall interaction belongs in the exclusion list, recorded as a
  code comment and a documented divergence per the gym↔game parity convention
  (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- Implement through the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`), never a divergent
  copy, so the game and every gym run the same code.
- Out of scope: boss behaviours, player ship, minerals, drops, and the bullet
  wrap model itself.
- Written in UK English per repo convention.

## Existing state

- Enemy aimed fire: `Scout.tryFireAimedBullet` computes
  `heading = atan2(target.y - y, target.x - x)` on **raw** positions with no
  seam consideration — the same aimed-shot method is reused for march and
  raider via `ENEMY_FIRE_METHODS` (`src/entities/enemyFire.ts`).
- Enemy bullets: wrap all four screen edges and expire by lifetime
  (AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0; shared bullet path in `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`).
- Enemy movement: bounded. Ghost/Grunt clamp to `GAME_WIDTH`/`GAME_HEIGHT`;
  march reverses and drops at arena bounds (`src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts`:
  `computeMarchBounds` / `advanceMarch`); centipede weaves within bounds;
  formation drift pushes rightward.
- Wrap model to match: player ship and `Asteroid.updatePosition` four-edge
  wrap; `Raider` patrol already wraps; `LaneTraffic` wraps horizontally.
- Enemies are data-driven: `EnemyConfig` (`src/core/configTypes.ts`) + seed
  defaults (`src/core/configDefaults.ts`) + CSV (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`)
  + enemy editor panel + gym editor.

## Desired change

1. Add the boolean parameter to `EnemyConfig` (`wrapAware`), seed default
   `true`; set `march` and `centipede` to `false`.
2. Seam-aware aim: for wrap-aware entities, compute the player delta along the
   shortest wrapped path before `atan2` in the shared aimed-fire seam; used by
   Scout / march / raider aimed fire (and any other archetype sharing the
   aimed-shot method).
3. Shared post-motion edge wrap: in the shared scene entity loop (game +
   gyms), wrap each wrap-aware enemy's position when it crosses an edge; gate
   on the flag so non-aware archetypes are untouched.
4. Verify per-archetype that nothing breaks (divers mid-dive, chasers,
   orbiters, swarm, formation drift) and adjust tests.
5. Update key docs (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; config-format
   docs if they enumerate fields).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add `wrapAware?: boolean` to `EnemyConfig`.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — seed defaults: `true` for most archetypes;
  `false` for `march` and `centipede`.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — new `wrapAware` column entries (if the CSV
  persists the field).
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` + aimed-fire call sites (`Scout.tryFireAimedBullet`,
  march, `Raider`) — seam-aware aim.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — expose the flag and any shared seam support.
- `src/scenes/core/` — shared post-motion wrap (CombatCoreScene / CombatScene
  shared entity loop, alongside the `enemyTargeting.ts` seams).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` + affected gym scenes
  (`GymFodderEnemies`, `GymCentipede`, …) — parity exercises.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — document the parameter and the
  exclusions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: gameplay feel** — seam-aware aimed fire lets shots come from
  unexpected directions; mitigated by limiting the change to aimed shots
  (radial/spread remain direction-symmetric) and excluding the classic
  archetypes.
- **Risk: wrap × state-machine interaction** — a post-motion wrap applied to
  every wrap-aware archetype could interact with steering that seeks the player
  or with dive/common state machines near the seam (oscillation). Mitigation:
  per-archetype verification during planning and dedicated unit tests at the
  seam.
- **Risk: formation-drift scope** — drift formations that push off-screen wrap
  at the entity level; formation *bases* and shaping logic stay as-is.
- **Scope-creep guard** — seam-aware spread/radial patterns (Q2 option b) are
  out of scope; if wanted later they are tracked as a new work item, not added
  here. Any extra archetype exclusion discovered during planning becomes a new
  work item or is documented as a divergence, not silent scope growth.
- **Assumption: config plumbing** — the parameter lives in `EnemyConfig`
  (CSV-backed, editor-editable), consistent with the established data-driven
  enemy tooling; default `true` for all archetypes except the explicit
  exclusions.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap
  around the screen" (completed). Bullets already wrap; this item builds
  directly on that model for launch direction.
- **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** — "Enemies should emerge from the wormhole" (open).
  Touches the same shared enemy spawn/motion seams; potential overlap to watch
  during planning.
- **AH-0MU4KQ6NT006MP52** — "Extract common enemy base class for regular
  enemies" (completed). `BaseEnemy` hosts the shared config/seam support.
- **AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN** — "Enemy Design tooling" (completed). The
  data-driven `EnemyConfig` pipeline this parameter extends.
- **AH-0MTAN4X5D009D7U6** — "Write ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md
  best-practice guide" (completed). The doc updated by AC 5.
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1** — gym↔game parity convention (referenced in
  `AGENTS.md`), enforced by `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Movement scope: which enemies should actually 'fly over the edge'? (a)
  All wrap-aware archetypes — shared post-motion wrap in scene loops;
  march/centipede excluded. (b) Firing only. (c) A curated subset."
  — Answer (Map): "(a)". Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Q2: "Firing scope: which fire patterns become seam-aware? (a) Aimed shots
  only. (b) All patterns."
  — Answer (Map): "(a)". Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.

# Audio Design Chapter — retro-arcade survival game GDD

## Problem statement

The GDD currently defines only SFX (§7.3 Audio Direction) and states background music is out of MVP scope with no musical direction defined. The game lacks a documented musical identity (scales, motifs, harmonic language, instrumentation, dynamic mixing, and state-driven music architecture) to guide composition and implementation when music is eventually built.

## Users

- **Audio designers and composers** — need a definitive musical language (scales/modes, motifs, progressions, instrumentation palette) to write consistent, on-brief music.
- **Technical audio programmers** — need the implementation contract (bus architecture, priority tiers, ducking, state machine, middleware guidance) to build or integrate the music system.
- **Game designers / producers** — need per-game-state emotional targets and transition rules to keep audio aligned with gameplay pacing.

User stories:

- As an audio designer, I want documented scales and motifs per game state, so my compositions match the game's emotional arc without guesswork.
- As a technical audio programmer, I want the music state machine and dynamic-mixing rules defined, so I can implement or configure the music engine against a fixed contract.
- As a producer, I want music explicitly scoped as design reference (out of MVP), so the shipped SFX scope (§7.3) is not disturbed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — New chapter file created:** An **AI Hell Music System** chapter is saved as a Markdown GDD addendum at `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`. Its **musical substance** is taken from the producer's original *Music & Thematic Audio Design* brief (Phrygian Dominant + Lydian scales; Combat Motifs A and B and the ambient "Star Drift" motif; the combat, boss and ambient progressions; the FM 2–4 operator + chiptune implementation notes — reproduced under **Source material (A)** below) and laid out in the **8-section + 2-appendix** professional structure of the approved reference brief (Ross, v1.0, 16 October 2026): **1** Audio Vision Statement; **2** Musical Identity (2.1 Tonal Language, 2.2 Core Motifs, 2.3 Chord Progressions); **3** Instrumentation Palette; **4** Dynamic Mixing Rules; **5** State-Driven Music Transitions (5.1 Transition Design Principles, 5.2 Transition Matrix, 5.3 Stinger System); **6** Implementation Guidelines (6.1 Audio Middleware, 6.2 Music Event Architecture, 6.3 Parameter Mapping Table, 6.4 Technical Specifications, 6.5 Audio Budget Table); **7** Composer and Sound Designer Briefs (7.1 Composer Brief, 7.2 Sound Designer Brief); **8** Audio Accessibility; **Appendix A** Motif Reference Sheet; **Appendix B** Glossary. The reference brief is a **structure exemplar only** — its Tableau card-game substance (D Dorian, harpsichord/cello ensemble, card-table SFX, parlour ambience) must **not** be imported into AI Hell's chapter.
- [ ] **AC2 — GDD §7.3 references the chapter:** The "Background Music" subsection in GDD §7.3 (Audio Direction) is updated to link the new chapter file, while retaining the explicit statement that background music is **out of MVP scope** (design reference only; SFX remains the only in-scope audio).
- [ ] **AC3 — GDD §8 future-scope row updated:** The "Background music" row in §8 (Future Scope) references the new chapter file so the doc stays self-consistent.
- [ ] **AC4 — Doc-only change, no behaviour impact:** No game code, SFX behaviour, or runtime audio pipeline is changed; existing §7.3 SFX scope and the shipped ToneForge pipeline remain authoritative for the MVP.
- [ ] **AC5 — Validation:** A new docs guard `src/audioDesignChapterDocs.test.ts` (following the sibling `*Docs.test.ts` convention, e.g. `src/powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts`) asserts, and passes, that: (i) `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists; (ii) it carries all 8 numbered sections plus Appendix A and Appendix B of the approved reference structure; (iii) GDD §7.3's "Background Music" subsection links the chapter **and** still states music is out of MVP scope; (iv) the GDD §8 "Background music" row links the chapter. All links resolve, and any index/table-of-contents entries are updated.
- [ ] **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (docs-only; confirms no accidental code impact).

## Constraints

- Music remains **"design reference, out of MVP scope"** — no change to the existing scope stance in GDD §7.3 or §8.
- The chapter is a **synthesis**, not a verbatim import (Q4/Q5, this session): the **musical content** is the producer's original retro-arcade brief reproduced faithfully (Source material (A)); the **document structure** follows the approved reference brief (author: Ross; version 1.0; dated 16 October 2026 — Source material (B)). The reference brief's Tableau card-game substance is **not** carried over.
- Follow the repo's docs naming/style conventions where sensible (singular Markdown addendum under `docs/`, referenced by relative link).
- UK English throughout.

## Existing state

- GDD §7.3 "Audio Direction" covers MVP SFX: baked ToneForge WAV pipeline, SFX event catalogue, per-enemy/per-player audio character, beat-synced explosion accents, and a one-paragraph "Background Music" subsection stating music is a nice-to-have, out of MVP.

```markdown
Music & Thematic Audio Design

This section defines the musical identity of the game, focusing on scales, motifs, harmonic language, and usage guidelines across gameplay states. The goal is to merge retro‑arcade space tension (Asteroids) with relentless survival energy (Vampire Survivors), using a coherent musical palette that supports procedural layering and dynamic intensity shifts.

🎼 1. Core Musical Identity

The soundtrack is built around two complementary scales:

Primary Combat Scale — Phrygian Dominant

Used for: wave combat, boss spawns, high‑intensity survival phases.

Scale Formula: 1 ♭2 3 4 5 ♭6 ♭7Example (E): E – F – G♯ – A – B – C – D

Why:

Retro‑arcade tension

Exotic, driving, instantly “space danger”

Works extremely well with FM bass, square leads, and arpeggiators

Provides strong melodic hooks with minimal notes

Secondary Ambient Scale — Lydian

Used for: menus, starfield travel, upgrade screens, low‑intensity exploration.

Scale Formula: 1 2 3 ♯4 5 6 7Example (C): C – D – E – F♯ – G – A – B

Why:

Bright, floating, cosmic

Contrasts the combat scale without breaking aesthetic cohesion

Ideal for pads, shimmering arps, and soft synth textures

🎵 2. Melodic Motifs

Motifs are intentionally short (2–6 notes) to support looping, procedural recombination, and chiptune‑style repetition.

Combat Motif A — “Incoming Wave”

Scale: Phrygian Dominant (E)Contour: Rising tension → abrupt dropNotes: E – F – G♯ – F – E – DUsage:

Triggered at the start of each enemy wave

Can be fragmented into E–F–G♯ for micro‑stingers

Works well as a 3‑note arpeggiated alert

Combat Motif B — “Survival Pulse”

Scale: Phrygian Dominant (E)Rhythmic Cell: Dotted + straightNotes: G♯ – A – G♯ – F – EUsage:

Mid‑combat loop

Easily reharmonized for intensity scaling

Can be doubled with FM bass for crunchy retro drive

Ambient Motif — “Star Drift”

Scale: Lydian (C)Contour: Floating, circularNotes: C – E – F♯ – E – D – CUsage:

Menu screens

Upgrade/shop interface

Slow arpeggiated background texture

🎹 3. Harmonic Progressions

Retro arcade music often avoids complex harmony, but these progressions provide structure while staying loop‑friendly.

Combat Progression (Phrygian Dominant)

E – F – E – D

Minimalist, modal, tense

Works with pulsing bass and rapid arps

Can be expanded to E – F – G♯ – F – E – D – C – D for boss phases

Boss Progression (Phrygian Dominant, extended)

E – C – D – F – E

Chromatic tension

Strong “danger escalation” feel

Supports heavy FM brass or distorted square leads

Ambient Progression (Lydian)

C – D – E – F♯

Bright, drifting, spacey

Works well with pads and slow-moving textures

Can be looped seamlessly or expanded to C – G – D – F♯

🔧 4. Implementation Notes

Motifs should be stored as atomic musical objects (interval sets + rhythm cells) for procedural recombination.

Combat layers should increase harmonic density (more voices, faster arps) rather than changing the motif.

Ambient layers should use long‑release envelopes and minimal rhythmic content.

FM synthesis (2–4 operators) and chiptune waveforms (square, triangle, noise) define the retro palette.

All motifs should be designed to loop cleanly at 1–2 bars for dynamic layering.
```

# Dev-mode write-back: gym "Save to repo" persists bot tuning to src/data/bot-tuning.json

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature

**discovered-from:** AH-0MV9GZD2C005IIU3 (its scope-creep note flagged this path out of scope there)

## Problem statement

Today the Bot Tuning gym persists only to `localStorage` (`ai-hell-bot-tuning`), and the Git-tracked shipped baseline `src/data/bot-tuning.json` must be refreshed manually via the gym **Export** button → overwrite file → commit (documented in `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §12 and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`). Player ship and enemy/difficulty configs already have a dev-mode write-back path: the Vite CSV plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`, served `/api/csv/...` PUT endpoints) writes gym Save/Save-As edits straight into the committed CSVs (`src/core/configStore.ts` `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`). This item gives bot tuning the same convenience: a dev-mode (Vite-serve-only) write path that persists the currently-selected tuning configuration to `src/data/bot-tuning.json`, so a designer does not have to Export → overwrite → commit manually.

## Users

- Designer tuning the demo bot in the Bot Tuning gym — wants a Save action that writes current tuning back to the committed baseline (dev server only).
- Maintainer / release reviewer — wants the write path dev-only and explicit, so a production/static build can never mutate the committed baseline.

Example user stories:

- *As a designer tuning the demo bot, I want a Save action in the Bot Tuning gym to write my current tuning back to `src/data/bot-tuning.json` (dev server only), so the shipped baseline stays in sync without the manual Export → overwrite → commit dance.*
- *As a maintainer, I want the write path to be dev-only and explicit, so a production/static build can never mutate the committed baseline or surprise a distributed user.*

## Desired change

1. **Write endpoint** — expose a dev-only endpoint (e.g. `PUT /api/bot-tuning/`) in the Vite dev-server plugin chain, mirroring the `configCsvPlugin` pattern (allowed-path allowlist, atomic write = temp file + rename, `apply: 'serve'` only). The endpoint validates the incoming blob's shape before writing (reuse the store's `parseState`-style validation / `coerceTuningValues`) and writes the exact `serialiseBotTuningState()` JSON blob to `src/data/bot-tuning.json`.
2. **Gym affordance** — add a "Save to repo" (dev-only) button in the Bot Tuning gym panel, next to Export, that posts the current store state to the endpoint and reports success/failure (`SaveResult`-shaped, like `saveShipConfig`). Disabled or hidden outside dev (`import.meta.env.DEV`, matching `saveShipConfig`'s `isDev()` gate).
3. **Out-of-scope guard** — no runtime behaviour change and no new write path in production; same guard contract as the CSV store (`WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` outside dev). Atomic replace must preserve the trailing-newline/pretty-print format the `bot-tuning.json` tests expect (`src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` asserts byte-identity with the store Export plus trailing newline).
4. **Tests** — unit tests for the write helper (valid blob replaces file; invalid blob rejected without touching the file; non-dev returns unavailable; byte round-trip with `serialiseBotTuningState()`), gym-level test that "Save to repo" calls the write path and reflects a real file write, and a plugin-endpoint test mirroring `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` scope. `npm run typecheck` and the full suite stay green; the gym↔game duplicate-body parity guard stays green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Dev-only write endpoint persists the baseline.** In dev mode, a write of the current `serialiseBotTuningState()` blob updates `src/data/bot-tuning.json` atomically; the file stays byte-identical to the store Export (pretty-print + trailing newline), so `src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` round-trip tests pass after the write.
- **AC2 — Invalid input never corrupts the file.** A write with an invalid/unschematised blob fails with a clear `SaveResult` reason and leaves the committed file untouched.
- **AC3 — Production/static builds cannot write.** The endpoint is dev-serve-only and the client gate (`isDev()`) means a production build reports `WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` (no mutation of the shipped baseline).
- **AC4 — Gym affordance.** The Bot Tuning gym exposes a dev-only "Save to repo" control that persists the current selection and reports success/failure; hidden/disabled outside dev.
- **AC5 — Tests + validation.** Unit + gym + plugin-endpoint tests cover persistence, rejection, round-trip, and non-dev unavailability; `npm run typecheck`, the full suite, and the parity guard pass.

## Constraints

- No change to bot decision/permission semantics — only a dev-tool persistence path (same scope boundary recorded in AH-0MV9GZD2C005IIU3).
- Follows the CSV plugin precedent exactly (atomic write, allowed-path allowlist, `apply: serve` only); do not invent a new infra pattern.
- The stored file must stay Git-committable and byte-stable (test contract).
- Out of scope: automatic background sync on every slider move (that would spam writes); the affordance must be an explicit Save action.
- Out of scope: any write path in production/static builds; dev-only via Vite serve.

## Existing state

- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` already exports `serialiseBotTuningState()` (the exact Export blob) and has `parseState`-style (private) schema validation + `coerceTuningValues` from `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`.
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` is the Git-tracked baseline whose byte-format contract is pinned by `src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` (pretty-print + trailing newline, byte-identical to fresh-profile Export).
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` is the established dev-write infra: `apply: 'serve'`, `/api/csv/...` GET/PUT, atomic write helper, allowed-path allowlist; registered in `vite.config.ts`.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` defines the `SaveResult` / `WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` / `isDev()` contract the bot-tuning write should mirror.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` already has the Export button/status readout in `_buildActionRow()` and the panel-status helpers; a "Save to repo" button slots in alongside.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — the CSV dev-write pattern to parallel/clone for bot tuning
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — the plugin-endpoint test harness to mirror
- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` — `serialiseBotTuningState()`, `parseState`/`coerceTuningValues` validation, `BOT_TUNING_SCHEMA_VERSION`
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig` + `SaveResult`/`WRITE_UNAVAILABLE` contract to mirror
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — the committed baseline the dev write targets
- `src/data/bot-tuning.test.ts` — file round-trip/trailing-newline contract the writer must preserve
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — new "Save to repo" control next to Export
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.test.ts` — gym-level write-path test
- `vite.config.ts` — plugin registration
- Docs: `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §12, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — update the refresh workflow (dev write vs Export)

## Related work

- `Distributed versions of the game do not use the correct Bot definitions (AH-0MV9GZD2C005IIU3)` — completed; introduced the bundled baseline this write-back refreshes; its scope-creep note explicitly deferred this dev-mode write path.
- `Gym scene for AI bot tuning (AH-0MV4D7LAD009XYR0)` — completed; the tuning gym + store.
- `Watch Demo and video recording should fly the saved bot-tuning configuration (AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL)` — completed; Export/`--bot-config` workflow.
- `Config store: in-memory registry, boot load, dev write (AH-0MUE2MGZM0016U3L)` / `Vite CSV plugin: dev middleware (GET/PUT, atomic write, validation) (AH-0MUE2MHRC0090AXP)` — completed; the CSV write-back precedent this item parallels.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "Save to repo" writes the full store state** (`serialiseBotTuningState()` blob, all named configs + current selection), i.e. exactly the Export blob. This is the only format the byte-identity test contract accepts (the shipped file is the whole `{ version, current, configs }` state), so the button's "current selection" phrasing means the current exported state. (If instead only the single selected config should be written, the file-format contract would need revisiting — not expected.)
- **Assumption — endpoint shape** follows the CSV-plugin precedent: a dev-only Vite middleware, PUT `/api/bot-tuning/` (or a parallel path under a bot-tuning prefix), validating before atomic write. Exact path is an implementation decision within the pattern.
- **Risk — stale baseline:** unchanged existing risk; the dev write reduces (does not eliminate) manual-drift by making the refresh an explicit action.
- **Risk — surprise writes:** a designer clicking Save expects a repo mutation; mitigations: dev-only gate, explicit button label + tooltip, `SaveResult` feedback.
- **Scope-creep risk:** automatic background sync on every slider move is out of scope (explicit Save only). Record any follow-up ideas as new work items, not scope.

## Verification of existing information

- Verified in repo: `serialiseBotTuningState()` is exported from `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` (byte-identical Export blob); `coerceTuningValues` exported from `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`; `parseStateObject` is private (a small store change or a plugin-local validator may be needed — implementation detail, not a requirement change).
- Verified in repo: `configCsvPlugin` exports `atomicWrite`, uses `apply: 'serve'`, allowed-path allowlist, and its test suite exercises PUT/atomic/validation via a real ephemeral HTTP server with `serve`/`build` modes — the exact harness to mirror.
- Verified in repo: `GymBotTuning._buildActionRow()` already builds Export + status; `GymPlayer._onSave()` shows the `saveShipConfig` status-reporting pattern to mirror.
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping item found (searches: "write-back", "save to repo", "config write"; the closest completed items are the CSV write-back precedent and the scoped-out parent note).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: None required — the seed context (detailed discovered-from description) sufficed to draft a clear brief; the repo confirms the referenced APIs and file-format contract. Assumptions above are flagged for producer confirmation rather than asked, per the intake rule to not ask answerable-by-repo questions.
- Open question (advisory, not blocking): endpoint shape — preferred option **parallel dev-only middleware mirroring `configCsvPlugin`** (explicit path, keeps CSV plugin untouched and its tests stable); alternative is extending the CSV plugin's allowlist (rejected: not a CSV, and would complicate the CSV plugin's schema).

# More Force Field feedback: persistent permanent bubble + intercept flash/SFX

## Problem statement

Two player-facing gaps in the Force Field (Gradius-homage reflector, AH-0MV1BIX1W006XF95):

1. **Bubble** — when the Force Field is **permanent** (hold-full reward), its bubble graphic disappears: it reads as if the temporary pickup timer removed it. This is a bug: `drawForceFieldBubble` (`src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts:304`) gates the draw on `registry.remaining('force_field')` — the **temporary window countdown**. A permanent-only field is stored with `remaining: 0` (`_startOrRefreshTimed`, `src/powerups/effects.ts:687`) and a permanent base whose temp window has expired is reset to `remaining = 0` (`_expireTimedEffect`), so the bubble is drawn for at most the temp window (base 8 s) and then cleared even though `isForceFieldActive()` is still true for the whole run.
2. **Intercept feedback** — when the field reflects a bullet there is no flash and no sound; the interception is easy to miss. `CombatScene._reflectEnemyBullet` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:1528`) only spawns the reflected bullet.

## Users

- As a player who has earned the permanent Force Field, I want the bubble to stay visible for the rest of the run, so I can read that my field is active.
- As a player, I want every intercepted bullet to flash and make a sound at the bounce point, so I can tell "the field ate that" from "I got hit".
- As a maintainer, I want the feedback to live once in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/` + shared helpers), so the game and every gym behave identically (gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).

## Existing state

- `EffectsRegistry` distinguishes **permanent** base effects from **temporary windows** on top (AC1/AC2 of the player force-field work): `_timed` entries carry `permanent`, `tempWindow`, `remaining`. A permanent-only field never counts down (`tick` skips it, `src/powerups/effects.ts:727-728`) and the HUD already renders it as `∞` via `powerUpTemporaryRemaining(id)` (returns `undefined` for a permanent base with no window).
- `drawForceFieldBubble` is already shared and called every frame by `PlayScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymFormationScene`; it pulses the rim continuously and brightens the fill in the final second of the countdown (mirroring the Shield bubble, AH-0MUAYB5HR001HDYC).
- Shared feedback precedents the fix should reuse:
  - `spawnBulletImpact` (`src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts`) — self-destroying flash with a trackable `registry`; origin AH-0MU43IIQV001S5JR; used by the enemy-force-field absorb seam (AH-0MVM8GW7W004SI0E AC3) and per-identity player-hit impacts (`_spawnEnemyBulletHitImpact`, `CombatScene.ts:1511`).
  - `playBulletDestructionSound` — the short bright "shatter" tick, already the deliberate choice for *absorb* feedback (Thorn Field `vfx/thornsAbsorb.ts`, AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T) and the enemy-field *break* cue (`playEnemyForceFieldBreakSound`, AH-0MVM8GW7W004SI0E); distinct from the player-hit boom.
  - `spawnEnemyForceFieldBreakFlash` — tween-based bubble burst (enemy side; not needed for the player field).
- The reflect branch is one shared loop in `CombatScene` (enemy bullets vs player, where `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()` succeeds); `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts:3260` pins `_reflectEnemyBullet` as shared, so feedback added there reaches the game and every gym with no scene edits.

## Desired change

1. **Permanent bubble persistence** — change the draw gate from `registry.remaining('force_field')` to the temporary-window semantics already used by the HUD: draw while `isForceFieldActive()` and there is either an active temporary window or a permanent base. Recommended implementation: gate on `powerUpTemporaryRemaining('force_field')` (`undefined` = permanent-only → draw with steady pulse, no countdown brighten/shrink; else existing countdown behaviour). Alternative: add an explicit `isForceFieldPermanent()` accessor. **Reflect-budget semantics are unchanged** (`_forceFieldRemaining` still caps reflections; exhausting the budget does not hide a permanent bubble — visual only; see Open question R1).
2. **Intercept flash + SFX** — in the shared reflect branch, on every successful `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()`:
   - spawn a short-lived flash at the intercept point via the shared impact seam (`spawnBulletImpact(this, x, y, { registry: this.bulletImpactEffects, color: FORCE_FIELD_COLOR })`), and
   - play the recorded audio cue.
   Recommended cue: reuse `playBulletDestructionSound` via a named `playForceFieldReflectSound()` export in `src/audio/effects.ts` (decision documented in the same way `playEnemyForceFieldBreakSound` and `thornsAbsorb` document theirs; no unrendered asset). Alternative: a new baked ToneForge cue (see Open question R2).

# AI should focus fire on the boss

## Problem statement

The attract/demo AI pilot does not prioritise the Central AI boss. The boss is
exposed to the bot as an ordinary combat target (`contentId: 'boss'`), but the
shipped competent-bot content registry has no `boss` profile, so
`resolveEnemy('boss')` falls back to the neutral default (`threat: 1`). The bot
therefore weights the boss exactly like a scout and keeps shooting whatever is
nearest — typically minions and hazards — during the encounter, so demo runs
rarely read as a deliberate boss fight.

## Users

- **Audience of attract/demo mode** — a viewer watching the demo reach the boss
  wants the pilot to visibly attack the boss.
  - *As a viewer, I want the demo bot to focus its fire on the boss so the
    finale reads as an intentional boss fight rather than incidental
    minion-clearing.*
- **Game designers / balancers** — need a discoverable, single-source knob for
  boss prioritisation rather than a hard-coded constant.
  - *As a designer, I want the boss weighting expressed once in the bot content
    registry and its priority band expressed once in the tunables, so I can
    retune the behaviour without editing framework logic.*
- **Bot maintainers** — need the behaviour to follow the existing content,
  goal-band and parity conventions.
  - *As a bot maintainer, I want the boss rule to apply to both the final boss
    and the per-level mini-bosses through the existing `boss` snapshot target.*

## Existing state (evidence gathered)

- The production AI is the structured competent bot: `PlayScene` constructs
  `createCompetentBotBrain()` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:571`). The legacy
  `decideBotIntent` path (`src/ai/botDecision.ts`) is only a framework fallback
  adapter and is not used by `PlayScene` — it is **out of scope** here.
- `buildBotSnapshot` exposes the boss as `{ x, y, alive, phase }`
  (`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:137`). `PlayScene.getBoss()` returns
  `this.miniBoss ?? this.boss` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4200`), so **mini-bosses
  and the final boss both arrive at the bot as `contentId: 'boss'`**.
- `enemyTargets()` appends `{ x, y, contentId: 'boss' }` to the live enemy list
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts:180`).
- The enemy engagement goal scores `base + span × proximity × threat`
  (`weightedUtility`), and the engage behaviour selects a target with
  `bestWeightedTarget` — `threat / (1 + distance)` — both using
  `content.resolveEnemy(contentId).threat`
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts:224`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts:114`).
- `COMPETENT_BOT_CONTENT` registers every spawnable enemy archetype but **no
  `boss` profile** (`src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts`), so the boss
  resolves to `DEFAULT_ENEMY_PROFILE` (`threat: 1`, `aim: 'direct'`, tunable
  engagement range of 140).
- Band arithmetic: `survivalBase 10`, `lifeBase 6`, `mineralBase 4`,
  `powerUpBase 3`, `enemyBase 2`, `asteroidBase 1`, `repositionBase 0.1`, with
  `prioritySpan 0.5`. A neutral-threat enemy band caps at **2.5**, so minerals
  and power-ups outrank combat today; a pure `threat: 2` boss reaches only
  **3.0** and still loses to minerals (4) and power-ups (3 + span).
- Target arithmetic: `weight / (1 + distance)` means a 2× boss beats a neutral
  enemy only while `1 + d_boss < 2 × (1 + d_enemy)` — roughly twice the
  competitor's distance. A minion at ~100 px still beats a boss at ~300 px (the
  usual boss standoff), so a content weight alone gives a **bias, not focus**.
- `BotBoss` exposes no `vx`/`vy`, so boss engagement aims at the current
  position rather than a lead (existing limitation; not changed here).

## Desired change

While a boss is alive and within the bot's enemy seek range, the bot makes the
boss its engagement target — regardless of nearer regular enemies — and keeps
firing at it instead of diverting to collection, with survival remaining the
only higher priority. The boss carries a weight of **2.0** (twice the neutral
enemy weight of `1`) in the content registry, and the boss-focus priority band
is expressed once in the competent-bot tunables.

Design sketch (the planner may refine details without changing intent):

1. **Content** — register a `boss` enemy profile
   (`{ id: 'boss', threat: 2, aim: 'direct', asteroidLike: false }`) in
   `COMPETENT_BOT_CONTENT`. Omitting `engagementRange` keeps the standoff
   single-sourced in `COMPETENT_BOT_TUNABLES`.
2. **Priority band** — add an `engage-boss` goal registered below `survive`
   (and `secure-life`) and above `collect-mineral`/`collect-powerup`, with a new
   `bossBase` tunable (e.g. 4.5, between `mineralBase` 4 and `lifeBase` 6). The
   goal is valid only while a live boss is inside the enemy seek range and is
   achieved/invalid when the boss dies or leaves range.
3. **Hard priority** — the `engage-boss` goal's target set is the boss alone, so
   the engage behaviour cannot pick a nearby minion. The boss stays in
   `enemyTargets()` (weighted 2.0) as the fallback when the boss band is invalid
   (e.g. out of range).
4. **Single source** — the weight lives in the content registry; the band base
   lives in `CompetentBotTunables` and is surfaced in the tuning fields and the
   bundled baseline like every other competent tunable.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Boss profile and weight.** `COMPETENT_BOT_CONTENT.resolveEnemy('boss')`
   returns a shipped profile with `threat === 2` (twice the neutral `1`),
   `aim === 'direct'` and `asteroidLike === false`; a shipped-registry test
   asserts these values, and the unknown-content fallback is unchanged.
2. **Boss-focus goal band.** A dedicated boss-engagement goal is registered
   below `survive`/`secure-life` and above `collect-mineral`/`collect-powerup`,
   with `.base` sourced from the competent tunables; it is valid only while a
   live boss is within the enemy seek range and invalid once the boss dies or
   leaves that range.
3. **Hard priority and sustained focus.** With a live boss inside the enemy
   seek range and a **nearer regular enemy** also in range, the bot's committed
   goal is the boss goal, the engage target is the boss, and the boss stays
   committed across consecutive ticks (no flip-flop to minions).
4. **Survival first, collection subordinated.** A threatening incoming shot
   still selects `survive` over the boss goal, while milestones/power-ups never
   divert the bot while the boss goal is valid.
5. **Scope.** The behaviour covers both the final boss and per-level
   mini-bosses, since both surface as the same `boss` target in `BotSnapshot`;
   a snapshot-level test exercises the boss target and documents that mini-boss
   parity.
6. **Single-source tuning and guards.** The boss weight is read from the content
   registry (no duplicated magic number in goals/behaviours); the new band base
   is added to `CompetentBotTunables`, `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` (with a
   tooltip), and the bundled baseline configuration; the competent-bot docs
   guard test is updated deliberately for the new goal id.
7. **Documentation.** `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` documents the boss profile in §11
   and the boss-focus band/priority order in §9 (including the `engage-boss` id);
   affected code comments are updated. CHANGELOG is excluded (release pipeline
   owns it).
8. **Validation gate.** The full project test suite passes with the new tests,
   run through `/skill:test` (repository test-execution policy); the new tests
   cover content, goals, behaviours and an integration scenario.

## Constraints

- **Content-first, core-light.** Prefer a content-registry entry for the weight;
  the new goal band is the minimum core change needed for hard priority and
  must follow the existing registry pattern (no `switch` on ids).
- **Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour lives in the shared competent brain, which
  the game and every bot gym consume — no divergent copy. `GymBotTuning` stubs
  `getBoss: () => null`, so it does not currently exercise boss engagement;
  adding a boss-capable bot gym is a non-blocking follow-up, not part of this
  change.
- **No gameplay changes.** Boss HP, phases, attack patterns, movement,
  mini-boss gating and boss VFX/audio are out of scope.
- **Read-only snapshot.** `BotSnapshot` stays read-only; no new mutation or
  scene coupling.
- **Tunables discipline.** Any new tunable must be added to
  `CompetentBotTunables`, `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` (with a tooltip) and the
  bundled baseline configuration, so the shipped tuning UI and docs stay in
  sync.
- **Legacy bot out of scope.** `src/ai/botDecision.ts` is not the production
  path; do not duplicate the rule there.
- **Scope creep.** General combat-over-pickups behaviour outside boss
  encounters, and boss aim-lead (needs `BotBoss` velocity), are separate work
  items rather than extra scope here.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts` — Add the `boss` profile
  (`threat: 2`, `aim: 'direct'`, `asteroidLike: false`).
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — Register the `engage-boss` goal, its
  validity/target set and the `COMPETENT_GOAL_IDS` entry.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — Handle the boss goal in the
  engage behaviour (boss-only target set / boss-first selection).
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — Add the boss-band base with a
  documented default.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/content.test.ts` — Shipped boss profile and
  weight assertions.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts` — Boss-vs-minion
  priority, sustained focus, survival pre-emption and pickup subordination.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBotDocs.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/contentDocs.test.ts` — Update the docs guards for the new
  goal id / boss content.
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`, `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — Surface and baseline the
  new band base.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — Document the boss profile (§11) and the boss-focus
  band/priority order (§9).
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4200` — Evidence only
  (boss/mini-boss exposure); no change expected.

## Related work

- **Demo bot movement goals: minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids**
  (AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L) — established the band ordering this change refines
  with a boss band above collection.
- **Structured competent bot: utility goals, behaviour tree, predictive
  dodge/aim** (AH-0MUY08WX3000ZEVO) — the goals/behaviours and docs guards this
  change extends.
- **Content-adaptive configuration** (AH-0MUY08X98002TRHT) — the content
  registry and its documented extension path.
- **Enemy classification system for balanced wave design**
  (AH-0MV29NWI1007NKN7) — origin of archetype threat/weight concepts.
- **Bot rotation skills** (AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98) — aim/lead handling reused by
  boss engagement.
- **Add figure-of-8 boss movement in shared core** (AH-0MUZMTS8J0029FSS) — the
  boss is a moving target; `BotBoss` still exposes no velocity.
- **Gym scene for AI bot tuning** (AH-0MV4D7LAD009XYR0) — stubs `getBoss: null`;
  boss-capable bot gym noted as a follow-up.
- **Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry**
  (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4) — the demo/attract context this improves.
- Docs: `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9 and §11; GDD §3.3 (mini-bosses) and §4.3
  (final boss).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** "the AI" means the attract/demo pilot (the competent bot
  brain), not enemy AI.
- **Assumption:** "boss level" covers every boss encounter, because the bot sees
  mini-bosses and the final boss through the same `boss` target (producer
  decision 3).
- **Risk — minion pressure:** hard boss focus means the bot ignores minions
  that are not an imminent survival threat; minions may accumulate. Mitigated by
  the existing survival goal and predictive-steering hazard avoidance, and by
  the tuning band (`bossBase`) if playtesting shows it is too absolute.
- **Risk — demo pacing:** killing the boss faster changes showcase and capture
  timing; acceptable, but capture/showreel scenarios may need retiming.
- **Risk — moving-boss accuracy:** without `BotBoss` velocity the bot aims at
  the current position, so hits on a fast figure-of-8 phase may be fewer than a
  human's. Exposing boss velocity is a follow-up.
- **Risk — docs-guard churn:** adding a goal id breaks the competent-bot docs
  guard until `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` lists it; the guard update is deliberate.
- **Risk — baseline drift:** a new tunable must be added to the bundled baseline
  and tuning UI, or the demo will run with a value the producer cannot see/tune.
- **Scope-creep guard:** general combat-over-pickups behaviour outside boss
  encounters and boss aim-lead become linked work items.

## Resolved decisions (producer)

- **Q1 — Meaning of "2x":** **A** — twice the neutral enemy weight, i.e.
  `boss.threat = 2.0` (not 2× the tank, no multiplicative code path).
- **Q2 — Bias vs priority:** **B** — hard priority: while the boss is alive and
  inside the enemy seek range it is the engagement target regardless of nearer
  regular enemies; survival still outranks.
- **Q3 — Collection and scope:** **B** — a dedicated boss band below survival
  and above collection, applying to both the final boss and per-level
  mini-bosses.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — What does "2x" mean as a weight?** (Options: A 2.0 vs neutral,
  B 2.8 vs tank, C multiplicative factor.)
  — **Answer (producer, interactive reply): A — 2.0, twice the neutral enemy
  weight.** Final accepted answer. Source: producer reply to
  AH-0MVBMESIE003YQ68 question comment; evidence: content registry contract in
  `src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts` (neutral default `1`).
- **Q2 — Weighted bias or hard priority?** (Options: A 2× bias, B hard
  priority, C hybrid.)
  — **Answer (producer, interactive reply): B — hard priority while the boss is
  alive and inside the enemy seek range, with survival higher.** Final accepted
  answer. Source: producer reply; evidence: `bestWeightedTarget` scoring in
  `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` and band ordering in
  `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`.
- **Q3 — Does focus fire outrank pickups, and does it include mini-bosses?**
  (Options: A enemy band only, B boss band above collection covering
  mini-bosses, C final boss only.)
  — **Answer (producer, interactive reply): B — boss band below survival and
  above collection, including mini-bosses.** Final accepted answer. Source:
  producer reply; evidence: `PlayScene.getBoss()` returns `miniBoss ?? boss`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4200`) and band bases in
  `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` (`mineralBase 4`, `lifeBase 6`).

Research basis for the options: inspected
`src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts`, `goals.ts`, `behaviours.ts`,
`tunables.ts`, `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` and `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4200`;
searched the worklog for prior boss/bot-targeting items (no duplicate found).

## Problem statement

The PlayScene integration test `PlayScene — Robotron homing horde (AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6) > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`) failed once during the AI_Hell full suite (heavy machine load) and passed on a fresh full-suite re-run minutes later with identical code. It is a flaky test, not a gameplay regression, and it is the last remaining kill test in this file that has not been hardened against non-deterministic scene state.

## Users

- **AI agents and producers running the full suite** — a red full-suite gate blocks `dev` pushes and triggers `test-failure` triage items and retries.
- **Developers of the Robotron horde (and shared kill seam)** — they need the horde kill/accounting contract to stay proven while the test stays stable.

Example user stories:

- *As an agent whose `implement.py finish` gate runs the full suite, I want the Robotron horde kill test to pass deterministically so that an unrelated docs-only change is never blocked by it.*
- *As a maintainer, I want the wave-accounting contract (a horde kill counted exactly once) still asserted, so the fix does not hide a real regression.*

## Existing state (evidence)

Failure from the `implement.py finish` gate for AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H (docs-only change, cannot affect kill behaviour):

```
FAIL |integration| src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once
AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6168:26
    6166|     scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
    6167|     scene.tick(0.001);
    6168|     expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
```

Same run also printed repeated `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000` on stderr (unrelated noise; no test failed on it).

The current test body (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6174-6184`) is:

```ts
const victim = liveGrunts(scene)[0];
scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
scene.tick(0.001);
expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
expect(wm.enemiesAlive).toBe(total - 1);
```

Two facts narrow the cause:

1. **The test is non-deterministic per run, independent of load.** `bootWithHordeWave()` never injects an RNG or run seed, so `PlayScene._initRunSeed()` draws a fresh `randomSeed()` (`Math.random()`, `src/core/rng.ts`) each run and the horde plan (`computeHordeSpawns`, `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts`) places the 16 grunts at RNG-jittered points along the four arena edges. The passing re-run therefore re-drew a different layout; "passed on re-run" is *not* evidence that load is the variable.
2. **The identical scenario has already been fixed one describe-block earlier.** `killing a pursuer advances wave accounting exactly once` (Pac-Man pursuer) had the same single-`tick(0.001)` shape and the same flake, and was fixed by wrapping the kill in the existing module-level `isolateEnemyForKill(scene, victim)` helper (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:397-410`, documented as AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK): it stubs `getEnemyEntities()` to the victim only and disables auto-fire for the duration, so "auto-fire or an overlapping pursuer cannot add a second kill and double-decrement the wave accounting". The Robotron horde kill test is the *unhardened sibling* of that test — it predates/omits the isolation.

The description's original hypothesis ("the physics/collision step for that tick may not process the new projectile before the assertion") is **not** supported: `scene.tick(dt)` is a synchronous call that runs the full player/auto-fire/bullet/collision/accounting pass in one go (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1265+`), so a longer tick cannot make a pass "complete"; what changes with a longer tick is *how much extra state* (auto-fire bullets, homing movement, wave timer) participates in that pass.

## Diagnosis to confirm during implementation

Confirm the exact mechanism before changing the assertion. Candidate mechanisms, in order of likelihood:

1. **Auto-fire / other-bullet interference** — the scene's auto-fire is live in this scenario, so a shot fired in the same tick can hit a grunt (or a different, overlapping grunt) and shift which entity the spawned bullet resolves against. The pursuer precedent (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) fixed exactly this with `isolateEnemyForKill`.
2. **Overlapping horde grunts** — grunts in one spawn group share an edge and can be placed close enough that a bullet placed on the victim is also within an earlier-iterated grunt's hit radius.
3. **Wave-phase/`paused` gating** — a wave-timeout transition switches `tick()` to the carried-survivor-only collision pass (`_handleCarriedSurvivorCollisions`), and a paused scene makes `tick()` a no-op; either would leave the victim alive. Check `scene.isTransitioning()` / `paused` under the failing seed.
4. **Wall-clock frames before the loop is stopped** — `bootScene()` resumes the live RAF loop, and `advanceGame()` stops it only after a microtask yield, so real frames with real deltas run before the deterministic stepping begins (load-dependent state drift). Relevant if the failure reproduces without seed isolation.

Reproduce deterministically (seed sweep): inject a fixed seed via `scene.setRng(createSeededRng(<seed>))` before `scene.restart()` and sweep seeds until the failure reproduces, then fix and verify that seed. Prefer the narrowest fix that removes the interference.

Steps to reproduce (seed sweep):

1. In `bootWithHordeWave()`, add `scene.setRng(createSeededRng(seed))` before `scene.scene.restart()` (import `createSeededRng` from `../core/rng`).
2. Loop seeds (e.g. `0..999`) in a temporary harness or repeated test-skill runs until `victim.alive` is `true` after the kill step; note the seed.
3. Record the seed and the observed mechanism on this work item, then apply the fix and re-verify that seed plus a broader sweep.

## Desired change

Make the horde kill test deterministic **without weakening what it proves**:

- Isolate the kill exactly as the pursuer test does — reuse `isolateEnemyForKill(scene, victim)` (`auto-fire` off, only the victim visible to the collision pass) — and/or pin the scene RNG to a fixed seed so the horde layout is reproducible.
- Keep the single-tick kill if it is deterministic after isolation; otherwise use a small bounded "tick until the victim dies" loop (guard counter, e.g. ≤ 20 frames of `0.016`) and assert the *outcome*.
- Still assert that the victim dies **and** that wave accounting drops by exactly one — and, to prove "exactly once", assert the accounting is unchanged after further ticks (no double decrement).

## Acceptance criteria

- The flaky failure is reproduced deterministically first (fixed seed and/or a temporary repeat-run harness), and the observed mechanism is recorded as a comment on this work item with the failing seed (or an explicit statement that no seed reproduces it, with the evidence gathered).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` passes on repeated runs: at least 20 consecutive runs of `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` via the test skill, and at least one run with an additional concurrent load-generating job active, all green.
- The test still proves the contract: the victim grunt is dead after the kill step, and `wm.enemiesAlive` is exactly `total - 1` (and stays `total - 1` after further ticks — a kill is never counted twice). The "exactly once" proof is not weakened to "at most once".
- The fix is confined to test code (plus test comments); no gameplay behaviour, RNG semantics, or `isSpawning`/collision logic changes. If investigation shows a genuine gameplay defect is being masked, stop and record it as a new work item (`discovered-from:AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU`) rather than loosening the test.
- If the fix pattern is reusable (e.g. other horde/pursuer kill tests), note it in the test comment referencing AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU and AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK so the next reader sees why the isolation is required.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Test-execution policy:** every agent-initiated test run goes through the test skill (`/skill:test`, `run_tests.py`) — no ad-hoc `vitest`/`npm test`. Repeated-run verification is therefore a test-skill invocation with a narrow scope (changed-scope gate) plus the full-suite gate at push.
- **No assertion weakening:** a longer tick alone is acceptable only if it is deterministic after isolation; it must not become a "sleep until it works" loop with an unbounded guard.
- **No production-code behaviour change:** the horde kill path (`_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies`, `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`) is shared with every gym (`src/scenes/core/`), so a behavioural change would require gym-parity work — out of scope unless a real defect is found.
- Prefer reusing existing helpers (`isolateEnemyForKill`, `finishSpawnSequence`) over introducing a new pattern.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — horde kill test at ~6174; `bootWithHordeWave`/`releaseHorde` helpers at ~6089-6124; existing `isolateEnemyForKill` helper at ~397-410 to reuse.
- `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts` — RNG-driven spawn placement (`computeHordeSpawns`) explaining per-run layout variance.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `planHordeSpawns` / `_releaseDueHordeSpawns` (~2164-2245), `tick` collision/phase ordering (~1265-1390), `_initRunSeed` (~4849-4863).
- `src/core/rng.ts` — `randomSeed()` / `createSeededRng()` (`Math.random`-seeded runs by default).
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — `bootScene`/`advanceGame` deterministic harness (frame-loop stop/resume behaviour).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies` (~1189) and `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` (~384) — read-only context for the interference analysis.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** no gameplay defect is being masked. If the isolated test still fails for a fixed seed, the flake may reflect a real horde/accounting bug — escalate as a new (child) work item instead of widening the tick.
- **Risk:** adding `scene.setRng(...)` in this describe block changes the RNG stream for the other four horde tests in the same block; keep the seed pinned in a `beforeEach`-style helper or per-test so assertions like "spawns the configured horde" stay valid.
- **Risk:** a bounded tick loop can hide a regression that makes kills take longer; keep the bound small (≈ 0.32 s simulated) and assert exactly-once accounting afterwards.
- **Risk (scope creep):** other single-tick kill tests in the same file (asteroids, boss phases) use `tick(0.016)` and have not flaked; do not refactor them wholesale — record as separate work if desired.
- **Risk:** flake attribution — a green re-run under load is weak evidence; the fix must be justified by a *reproduced deterministic* failure, not by "it passed 20 times".
- **Risk:** `isolateEnemyForKill` stubs `getEnemyEntities` and `autoFireEnabled` on the instance and must be restored in a `finally` block (as the pursuer test does); a leaked stub would silently affect later tests in the same file.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK** (completed) — `[test-failure] PlayScene — flaky wave-accounting kill tests (Harvester + Pac-Man pursuer)`; introduced `isolateEnemyForKill` for exactly this interference class. Direct precedent.
- **AH-0MUNVVWWC0015JTM** (completed) — `Flaky tests: PlayScene and GymFormationScene fail intermittently under full-suite parallel load`; load-sensitivity remediation (deterministic boot/frames).
- **AH-0MV5JRAH90034PKR** (completed) — `Flaky Centipede chain bounds assertion under full-suite load`; fixed "advanced 20 s in one tick" by stepping in 0.05 s increments — precedent for tick-size fixes in this file.
- **AH-0MVFPMT4P005UHZL** — removed the last wall-clock waits from the suites (`advanceGame` / `stepGameUntil`); the deterministic harness this test relies on.
- **AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6** — the Robotron homing horde feature these tests cover.
- **AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H** (completed) — docs-only change whose gate surfaced this flake (`discovered-from`).
- `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` — repo guard documenting the flake history and the supported deterministic replacements.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (agent consideration):** "Is the failure load-induced (wall-clock frame drift) or seed-induced (random horde layout)?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence, no producer input needed):** seed-induced is demonstrable from the code — `bootWithHordeWave` injects no RNG, so `_initRunSeed()` draws `randomSeed()` per run and `computeHordeSpawns` places grunts at RNG-jittered edge positions. The pass-on-re-run therefore used a different layout. Load may additionally drift scene state via live RAF frames before `advanceGame` stops the loop, but that is not required to explain the flake. Source: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4849-4863`, `src/core/rng.ts:49`, `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts` (`computeHordeSpawns`).
- **Q (agent consideration):** "Does the description's proposed fix (`scene.tick(0.05)` / tick-until-dead) actually address the mechanism?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence):** only partially. `scene.tick(dt)` is synchronous, so "the collision step did not process the projectile" cannot happen; the pursuer precedent (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) shows the real interference was auto-fire / overlapping entities, fixed by `isolateEnemyForKill`. The brief therefore requires isolation (plus a fixed seed) as the primary fix, with a bounded tick loop only as a secondary robustness measure.
- **Q (agent consideration):** "Should the fix change gameplay code (e.g. horde collision ordering)?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo constraints):** no. Any gameplay change is shared with every gym and would require gym-parity work; a genuine defect would be filed as a new work item instead. Assumption recorded in *Risks & assumptions*.
- **Producer input:** none required — the item's goal and acceptance criteria are unambiguous and the remaining decisions are resolved by repo evidence and precedent. Recorded here for auditability; no open questions.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUJRVYWG006NJUU** – Shared multi-hit kill finalisation (completed) — the shared kill seam this test's bullet path runs through.
- **AH-0MUIGTRFY002JDDS** – Shared mineral kill-drop helper + PlayScene/BaseEnemy refactor (completed) — touches the same enemy-kill finalisation path.

### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — gym↔game parity convention (§5.1), relevant to the "no behaviour change" constraint.
- `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` — documents this flake family and the supported deterministic replacements.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — `isolateEnemyForKill` helper (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) reused by the fix.
